description: Questions that work for any professional role, in any field.

questions.text: Tell me about yourself.
Walk me through your background.
Give me the short version of your career so far.
follow_up_angles: which part of that matters most for this role
questions.notes: Short-window variant. Good for practising stopping early.

questions.text: What should I know about you that isn't on your resume?
How would the people you work with describe you?
follow_up_angles: give me an example of that
questions.notes: Self-description, not a past example, so typed tell_me_about_yourself.

questions.text: In a sentence or two, what are you known for?
follow_up_angles: what are you not known for

questions.text: What's your biggest strength?
follow_up_angles: where has that strength gotten you into trouble

questions.text: What's your greatest weakness?
follow_up_angles: what are you doing about it now
questions.notes: No enum type for self-assessment; tell_me_about_yourself is closest. Not a past-example question.

questions.text: Is there anything we haven't covered that you'd want me to know?
follow_up_angles: why does that matter for this role
questions.notes: Closing prompt. Tests whether the candidate fills a gap in the evidence instead of repeating.

questions.text: Why are you interested in this role?
Why this company?
follow_up_angles: what do you know about what we're building

questions.text: Why are you leaving your current job?
questions.notes: Must stay positive and consistent across stages (C1).

questions.text: What are you looking for in your next role?
follow_up_angles: what would make you say no

questions.text: Where do you see your career going over the next few years?
follow_up_angles: how does this role get you there

questions.text: What kind of work gives you the most energy?
What would make you turn down an offer from us?
follow_up_angles: what would make you say no

questions.text: Why should we hire you over the other people we're talking to?
follow_up_angles: what would the other candidates say about you
questions.notes: Typed motivation as closest; it is really a positioning close. Classifier may pick tell_me_about_yourself.

questions.text: Why did you move from your last role to your current one?
follow_up_angles: what would make you say no

questions.text: You've moved around a fair bit. What's behind that?
follow_up_angles: why would this one be different

questions.text: What's most important to you in your next role: scope, pay or flexibility?
follow_up_angles: if you had to give one up, which

questions.text: Are you looking for a full-time role, doing your own thing, or both?
follow_up_angles: how much time does the side work take
what happens to it if you join
questions.notes: Founder opener. Passes only if the full-time goal comes first.

questions.text: Do you have anything going on the side right now? How much of your time does it take?
follow_up_angles: would that change if you joined

questions.text: If this works out, how long do you see yourself here?
follow_up_angles: what would make you say no

questions.text: Early-stage companies are messy. Why do you want that instead of something stable?
follow_up_angles: have you actually worked somewhere like that

questions.text: Are you a builder or an operator?
questions.notes: Typed tell_me_about_yourself as closest (self-description). Scored on the literal answer first, then an operator example.

questions.text: Are you more of a systems person, or do you run things day to day?
follow_up_angles: when did you last run something yourself
what did you change week to week
questions.notes: Rewording of builder vs operator, the way it is often asked in practice.

questions.text: Once something's built, do you stay and run it until the number moves, or hand it off?
follow_up_angles: how long did you run it
what did you change along the way

questions.text: Tell me about something you personally ran, week after week, until a number moved.
follow_up_angles: what did you change each round

questions.text: We need someone who'll do the unglamorous work too. What's the least glamorous thing you've owned recently?
follow_up_angles: why did you take it on

questions.text: What would you do if you disagreed with a call I made as the founder?
follow_up_angles: and if I still said no

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to build something with no process and no team around you.
follow_up_angles: what did you decide not to build
how did you know it was working

questions.text: What's your notice period?
When could you start?
follow_up_angles: is anything else holding that date

questions.text: What salary range are you targeting?
follow_up_angles: where in that range would you land
questions.notes: Must be answered plainly the first time, with a range decided in advance.

questions.text: Where are you based, and are you open to coming into the office?
follow_up_angles: how many days a week works

questions.text: Are you able to work here without sponsorship?
Are you interviewing anywhere else right now?
How many years have you worked in this field?
follow_up_angles: how many of those at this level

questions.text: What's your current title, and who do you report to?
follow_up_angles: what does that title mean in practice

questions.text: How big is the team you work with today?
follow_up_angles: who do you work with most

questions.text: Would you consider a contract to start, with a view to full-time?
follow_up_angles: what would you need to say yes

questions.text: How did you hear about this role?
Tell me about a time you solved a problem nobody had asked you to fix.
follow_up_angles: how did you measure the fix

questions.text: Walk me through the hardest problem you've worked on in the last year.
follow_up_angles: what did you try first that didn't work

questions.text: Give me an example of a time something broke and you had to fix it fast.
follow_up_angles: how did you find out it broke

questions.text: Tell me about a time the obvious answer turned out to be wrong.
Tell me about a decision you had to make without enough information.
follow_up_angles: what did you do to reduce the risk
would you make the same call today

questions.text: Tell me about a project that failed. What happened?
follow_up_angles: what was your part in it failing

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to choose between two priorities that both mattered.
follow_up_angles: how did you explain that to the people affected

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you cut cost or effort without hurting the result.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager.
Tell me about a time you pushed back on a request from someone senior.
Give me an example of a conflict with a peer and how it got resolved.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision but went along with it anyway.
follow_up_angles: how did you commit to it

questions.text: Tell me about a time someone pushed back hard on your idea.
Tell me about a time you had to say no to someone important.
Tell me about a time you got people to change how they worked without having any authority over them.
Tell me about a time you had to convince leadership to fund or prioritize something.
follow_up_angles: what was the case you made
what did they push back on

questions.text: Give me an example of using data to change someone's mind.
follow_up_angles: what if they'd still said no

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to get several teams to agree on one plan.
follow_up_angles: who had the most to lose
how did you keep them aligned after

questions.text: Tell me about a time you sold an idea people were skeptical about.
Tell me about a time you went out of your way for a customer.
Tell me about a time you had to deal with an unhappy customer or client.
Give me an example of customer feedback changing what you did.
Tell me about a time you had to tell a customer something they didn't want to hear.
Tell me about a time what customers actually needed turned out to be different from what they asked for.
Tell me about a time you led a team through a hard stretch.
Tell me about a time someone on your team wasn't performing. What did you do?
follow_up_angles: how long did you wait to act

questions.text: Give me an example of someone you helped grow in their role.
Tell me about a project you led where none of the people reported to you.
follow_up_angles: how did you keep people accountable

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to deliver bad news to your team.
follow_up_angles: what did you do the next day

questions.text: Tell me about a time you handed off work you cared about so the team could scale.
follow_up_angles: what did you have to let go of
how did you make sure it held up

questions.text: Tell me about a time you kept a long project going when nobody was paying attention to it.
Tell me about the piece of work you're proudest of.
Tell me about a time you took on something well outside your job description.
follow_up_angles: what did you give up to do it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to learn something new quickly to get the job done.
follow_up_angles: how good are you at it now

questions.text: Tell me about a time you lost interest in a project. How did you handle it?
follow_up_angles: what did you learn about yourself

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to deliver under a very tight deadline.
follow_up_angles: would you do it the same way again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to adapt to a big change at work.
Tell me about a time you got feedback that was hard to hear.
Tell me about a time you had to choose between doing it right and doing it fast.
follow_up_angles: what happened later because of it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to follow a rule or process you didn't agree with.
follow_up_angles: did you try to change it
what did you do in the meantime

questions.text: Tell me about a mistake you made that affected other people.
How do you decide what to work on first when everything feels urgent?
questions.notes: Method question, typed technical per prompt 01 (how the candidate works), not behavioral.

questions.text: How do you measure whether your work is actually making a difference?
follow_up_angles: what would it look like if it wasn't working

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd plan a project starting from a blank page.
follow_up_angles: what do you do before anything else
where do plans like that usually go wrong

questions.text: A number that matters dropped last month. How would you figure out why?
follow_up_angles: what if the data itself is wrong
who would you talk to first

questions.text: How do you document your work so someone else can pick it up?
follow_up_angles: has anyone actually picked it up
how do you keep it current

questions.text: If you had to cut your team's workload by a third tomorrow, how would you decide what goes?
How do you know when something is good enough to ship?
follow_up_angles: how would you know it worked

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd run a test to decide between two options.
follow_up_angles: how long would you run it
what if the result is flat

questions.text: How do you keep track of a lot of projects at once without dropping things?
follow_up_angles: how would you know it worked

questions.text: How would you set up a weekly report on your area for leadership?
follow_up_angles: what decision would it help them make

questions.text: How do you check your own work before it goes out?
What would your first 90 days look like?
If you joined, what's the first thing you'd want to understand?
follow_up_angles: what would you need to validate first

questions.text: Based on what you've seen so far, what would you change about how we do things?
follow_up_angles: what if you're wrong about that

questions.text: A year from now, what would make this hire a clear success, in your view?
follow_up_angles: what would get in the way

questions.text: Given the challenge I just described, where would you start?
follow_up_angles: what would you need to see first
questions.notes: Best with a JD or a described challenge loaded; without one the app should state a generic challenge first.

questions.text: How would you build trust with the team in your first month?
follow_up_angles: what would you need to validate first

questions.text: What do you think will be hardest about this role?
Have you managed people directly?
Have you worked in our industry before?
follow_up_angles: what would you have to learn

questions.text: This role is a step up from what you do now. What makes you ready for it?
Have you owned a budget?
follow_up_angles: how did you decide where it went

questions.text: Have you presented to executives or a board?
What questions do you have for me?
questions.notes: Candidate's-own-questions moment. No type in the enum fits a prompt that hands the floor to the candidate; typed motivation as closest (it shows interest and preparation). The spoken reply is scored by question_quality (prompt 10), not the normal rubric.

questions.text: Before we wrap up, is there anything you'd like to ask me?
questions.notes: Candidate's-own-questions moment. No type in the enum fits a prompt that hands the floor to the candidate; typed motivation as closest (it shows interest and preparation). The spoken reply is scored by question_quality (prompt 10), not the normal rubric.

questions.text: What would you want to know from me before deciding this is right for you?
questions.notes: Candidate's-own-questions moment. No type in the enum fits a prompt that hands the floor to the candidate; typed motivation as closest (it shows interest and preparation). The spoken reply is scored by question_quality (prompt 10), not the normal rubric.
